identified patient risks linked to how advice and guidance (A+G) services have been implemented acrossEngland.A+G was brought in to slash unnecessary hospital visits and reduce waiting times, allowing family doctors to seek specialist input before making referrals.The service has “positively influenced patient care” by improving communication betweenGPsand consultants, and “enabled efficient specialist input into care”, the HSSIB said.However, the investigation found evidence that A+G had “contributed to near misses and incidents of patient harm, both physical and psychological” where it had been poorly implemented or monitored.NHS to use AI on its app to direct patients to appropriate servicesRead moreThe report said “harm had arisen as a result of delayed or missed diagnoses, and delays to care and treatment”.It added: “Evidence demonstrated that A+G services were being used in some pathways where general practice had requested specialist assessment for suspected cancer.“Incidents demonstrated that this had contributed to delays in diagnosis.”Gaps in how systems were being implemented were also found.For example, some local pathways required GPs to use A+G instead of making direct referrals, or referrals were rejected despite persistent concerns from family doctors.The HSSIB recommended that NHS England and the Department ofHealthand Social Care rapidly evaluate A+G services to address resource and capacity gaps, training needs and weaknesses in reporting patient safety incidents.Dr Nick Woodier, a senior safety investigator at the HSSIB, said: “A+G services are making a real difference for patients in many parts of theNHS, and we heard genuine enthusiasm for what they can achieve.“But we also heard serious concerns, and found evidence of harm where implementation has not been adequately designed or monitored.“Our recommendations are about ensuring that expansion happens safely with the right support, standardisation and oversight in place to ensure patient safety is a priority.”A spokesperson for NHS England said: “As HSSIB acknowledges, advice and guidance has positively influenced patient care by reducing waiting times and giving people quicker access to specialist advice, but we know more needs to be done to make it work even more effectively.“That is why we’re giving GPs and hospitals clear guidance and practical tools to help deliver the service safely, consistently and effectively across the NHS, and have already commissioned an evaluation of its impact which will be published this year.”The HSSIB report followed a survey of 712 GPs by Pulse that found about a quarter of patient referrals are being rejected and returned as unsolicited A+G.Family doctors also estimated that 36% of the A+G they received asked them to do work considered outside their remit, and others raised concerns that the process is creating waits for people with suspected cancer.Dr Clare Bannon, the GPs’ committee chair at the British Medical Association, said: “Since its introduction, GPs have expressed deep concern with the advice and guidance system – we know our patients and know when a referral needs to be made. So this report is tragic vindication for these concerns, now showing that patients have come to harm as a result of this rushed-out and inconsistently applied process.“Just this week we had GPs telling a survey that a quarter of referrals were being sent back as advice and guidance, while genuine advice and guidance requests were taking 10 days or more for a response.“We know the pressures our colleagues in secondary care are facing and it’s clear that this process is not working for either of us, nor our patients.“The HSSIB is right to recommend an urgent evaluation of the advice and guidance system to address these clear patient safety risks.”Explore more on these topicsCancerGPsNHSHealthEnglandnewsShareReuse this content

title: US senator Jon Ossoff condemns Trump as ‘draft-dodging, crook president’ | Donald Trump | The Guardian
description: Potential presidential hopeful running for re-election in Georgia intensifies White House feud after remarks about ‘Natalie’ drew ire of president and allies
Author: Cecilia Nowell
Headline: Potential presidential hopeful running for re-election in Georgia intensifies White House feud after remarks about ‘Natalie’ drew ire of president and allies
Content: Jon Ossoff at a rally in Atlanta on Sunday.Photograph: Robin Rayne/Zuma/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenJon Ossoff at a rally in Atlanta on Sunday.Photograph: Robin Rayne/Zuma/ShutterstockDonald TrumpUS senator Jon Ossoff condemns Trump as ‘draft-dodging, crook president’Potential presidential hopeful running for re-election in Georgia intensifies White House feud after remarks about ‘Natalie’ drew ire of president and alliesCecilia NowellTue 18 Aug 2026 19.32 EDTLast modified on Tue 18 Aug 2026 19.50 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Democratic senator Jon Ossoff calledDonald Trumpa “draft-dodging, crook president” while defending the senator Mark Kelly as a hero during a Tuesday campaign appearance in Georgia, escalating his public feud with the US president.“I don’t think anything illustrates the times more aptly than that the draft-dodging, crook president, who has plunged our nation recklessly into a war he knows not how to end or to win, tried to imprison this man, who embodies American heroism,” Ossoff said while appearing alongside Kelly and his wife, the former Arizona congresswoman Gabrielle Giffords.White House launches personal attack on CNN reporter over question to TrumpRead moreKelly, a former navy captain, and five other Democratic lawmakers were attacked by Trump last year after they released a social media video saying troops are not required to carry out illegal commands.Trump called for the lawmakers’ arrests, accusing them of “SEDITIOUS BEHAVIOR, punishable by DEATH!”Ossoff, who is currently running for re-election to his Senate seat inGeorgiaand is widely speculated to be eyeing a 2028 presidential run, has received viral attention on social media for his sharp criticism of Trump.On Sunday, during a campaign appearance in Atlanta, Ossoff similarly attacked Trump’s handling of the US-Israel war on Iran.“While the sailors on the Lincoln fight his war, while he fruitlessly drains our munitions and oil reserves, the president sleeps through his meetings,”Ossoff said. “He golfs and trades stocks. See, he doesn’t want to do the job. He wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie on their apparently defenseless flying palace gifted by the amir of Qatar.”Ossoff appears to have been referring to Natalie Harp, Trump’s executive assistant, who has drawn scrutiny for her closeness to the US president.The White House quickly criticized Ossoff on Monday, with the president calling him “Pee-wee Herman” and the White House communications director, Steven Cheung, writing on social media that Ossoff is “a radical, extremist Dumocrat”.Explore more on these topicsDonald TrumpGeorgiaDemocratsUS SenateUS CongressUS politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: ABC sues Trump’s media regulator over demand for TV license renewals | Donald Trump | The Guardian
description: Network alleges FCC demand for early license renewal is retaliation for content the administration disapproves of
Author: Jeremy Barr
Headline: Network alleges FCC demand for early license renewal is retaliation for content the administration disapproves of
Content: Brendan Carr, the FCC chair, has ordered the network to apply early to renew eight local television stations’ licenses.Photograph: Daniel Cole/ReutersView image in fullscreenBrendan Carr, the FCC chair, has ordered the network to apply early to renew eight local television stations’ licenses.Photograph: Daniel Cole/ReutersDonald TrumpABC sues Trump’s media regulator over demand for TV license renewalsNetwork alleges FCC is trying to send ‘chilling message’ in retaliation for content the administration disapproves ofJeremy Barrin WashingtonTue 18 Aug 2026 09.38 EDTFirst published on Tue 18 Aug 2026 09.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleABChas sued the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), arguing that it is being retaliated against for content-based reasons in a move it warns threatens the independence of the press.The network filed the lawsuit on Tuesday after being forced to apply early to renew its license to broadcast on the eight local television stations it owns. It is waiting to hear whether theBrendan Carr-led FCC approves its renewal requests, or, more likely, holds a hearing on their merits.Late last month, a group of prominent former FCC officials, including key staffers and commissioners appointed by both Democratic and Republican presidents, issued a warning –in a filing– that the agency is trying to send a “chilling message” to broadcasters after forcing ABC to apply early.Conservative organizations, including the Center for American Rights and the Media Research Center,filed petitionsurging the FCC to deny the renewals, arguing that the network’s journalism is politically biased. ABC also still faces an FCC investigation over the daytime talkshow The View for a potential violation of equal time rules, an inquiry that remains open.ABC argues that early license review by FCC is ‘retaliation’ for network’s coverageRead more“Acting through the Federal Communications Commission, the Administration has waged a retaliatory campaign againstABCfor a single reason: it disapproves of what ABC broadcasts,” the network said in the suit, filed on behalf of its eight local stations in district court for the District of Columbia.“That campaign began in this Administration’s earliest days and has only intensified since. Again and again, the Administration has attacked ABC’s speech – the stories its journalists report and the viewpoints its network programs air. Over time, those attacks have escalated into express demands that ABC be stripped of its broadcast licenses because of its speech.”The lawsuit makes clear that ABC does not expect the FCC to renew its licenses, posing an existential threat to the network.“The Commission is poised to make good on its threat any day now: the public comment period on the renewal applications has closed, and the Commission may, at any moment, issue an unprecedented Hearing Designation Order for all eight Stations, which would kick off a formal agency adjudication to determine the fate of ABC’s licenses.”The network said that any adjudication process over its licenses would be a “charade”, particularly because the agency cannot, by statute, grant license renewals several years early.“The Commission cannot lawfully grant renewal this early in the license terms – the only outcomes on the table are adverse to Plaintiffs,” the network said in the lawsuit, expressing concern that the FCC would either “prolong” the process, “miring ABC in years of costly litigation”, or deny it altogether.“In either scenario, the Administration accomplishes its goal of eliminating a perceived media critic: either it gets Plaintiffs to fall in line, or it silences them if they refuse,” the plaintiffs argued.ABC’s lawyers argued that, if left unchecked, theTrump administrationwould have the ability to retaliate against any media company they dislike for editorial and political purposes. “If the Administration gets its way, the message to every media company in the country will be unmistakable: tell only the stories the Administration deems favorable, or face the coercive machinery of the federal government,” they wrote. “In such a world, the press could in no way be described as free.”The network asked the court to stop the FCC from taking any actions against it or threatening any actions against it.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toBusiness TodayGet set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morningEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe Guardian has approached ABC for comment on the lawsuit.An FCC spokesperson said: “All broadcasters have a legal obligation to operate in the public interest—even Disney. The FCC has been examining claims that Disney engaged in illegal DEI discrimination for over a year. Disney is obviously very concerned about the FCC’s proceeding, as evidenced by their ongoing campaign of disinformation as well as their decision to ask a court to stop the FCC from further pursuing matters. The FCC will continue to follow the facts and law wherever they lead.”Trump sued over $100,000-a-month early-access offer to Truth Social postsRead moreAnna M Gomez, the lone Democrat on the FCC, issued a statement commending ABC for filing suit against the agency. (Gomez was included as a defendant in the case.)“For months, the FCC has waged a campaign of censorship and control against Disney’s ABC stations, using the threat of broadcast license revocations to punish a company for speech this administration doesn’t like. I have long called on companies to push back against this kind of government intimidation, and I’m glad Disney has shown courage and stepped up. This should be a welcome sign for every broadcaster who has felt the weight of this overreaching government pressure in silence,” she said.“I am hopeful that this will mark the beginning of the end of this administration’s disregard for the Constitution and the law, and that the coming months will bring the costly legal defeat this agency has been asking for since it started down this path.”Explore more on these topicsDonald TrumpABCUS television industryTrump administrationUS politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Oil prices jump after US-Iran ceasefire expires and Trump threatens Oman | Oil | The Guardian
description: Brent crude rises above $90 a barrel for the first time since 30 July after US president tells Tehran to surrender
Author: Alex Daniel
Headline: Brent crude rises above $90 a barrel for the first time since 30 July after US president tells Tehran to surrender
Content: A ship anchored in the strait of Hormuz near Larak Island, Iran.Photograph: Majid Saeedi/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenA ship anchored in the strait of Hormuz near Larak Island, Iran.Photograph: Majid Saeedi/Getty ImagesOilOil prices jump after US-Iran ceasefire expires and Trump threatens OmanBrent crude rises above $90 a barrel for the first time since 30 July after US president tells Tehran to surrenderBusiness live – latest updatesAlex DanielTue 18 Aug 2026 07.50 EDTFirst published on Tue 18 Aug 2026 03.04 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleOil prices have risen again after the two-month window to negotiate a peace deal in theUS-Israel war on Iranexpired on Monday with no end to the conflict in sight.Iran said on Monday that it would take a more aggressive stance if talks with the US failed, while Donald Trump demanded Tehran “put up the white flag of surrender” in an interview with Fox News.Trump also threatened to bomb Oman if it “gets in the way” of his effort to end the war, the second time he has directed such a threat at the longtime US strategic partner. “If Oman gets in the way, we’ll bomb the shit out of them,” Trumptold Fox Newson Monday.Oil prices rise as US-Iran ceasefire ends; UK wage growth slows amid cost of living squeeze – business liveRead moreBrent crude rose above $90 a barrel for the first time since 30 July, and was trading at $91.63 on Tuesday morning.Angeline Ong, a senior technical analyst at the investing and trading platform IG, said: “Trump’s threat to bomb Oman could be the moment the oil market shifts from pricing a temporary disruption to pricing a prolonged one.“If Muscat pulls back from talks with Tehran, the diplomatic route to restoring normal flows through Hormuz narrows considerably. That would be a signal to add to energy longs rather than fade the rally – with roughly a quarter of global seaborne oil normally passing through the strait, even a small reduction in the probability of reopening warrants a higher geopolitical premium in crude.”Graph showing changing oil priceA cargo ship was attacked while travelling through the strait early on Tuesday, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency, after an Iranian official told Reuters that it would shift to a “fully offensive” military stance.Fox News reported on Tuesday that the Iranian military spokesperson Ebrahim Zolfaghari said vessels attempting to pass through the strait would “find several beautiful holes in their hulls”.Just six commodity ships travelled through the waterway on Monday, according to Kpler, a ship tracking company. That was slightly up compared with the weekend, when five ships transited on Saturday and Sunday combined.Analysts at Deutsche Bank wrote on Tuesday that the rising oil prices were a sign of investors pricing in “a more extended closure” of the strait.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toBusiness TodayGet set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morningEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionTrump made the threat against Oman as hestruggles to draw the conflict to a closealmost six months after it began. But the US president also claimed during Monday’s interview that he was “not in a hurry” to reach a deal.He has repeatedly claimed the war would end “soon”, and talked up the prospect of a lasting peace deal in recent months, without such a breakthrough materialising. Trump said he would not impose a fresh deadline on Iran, adding: “I have no time schedule. I’m not in a hurry.”Dan Alamariu, the chief geopolitical strategist at the research company Alpine Macro, warned that if there was no end to the fighting in the Middle East, energy prices could see a “double whammy” from that combined withRussia’s ongoing war in Ukraine.He said: “Escalation from September through November is likely and could deliver a double shock … even if a bigger two-war convergence remains just a tail risk.“Energy market risks will persist, and oil and gas prices and volatility would spike with another bout of sustained, intense conflict, especially in the Gulf.”Explore more on these topicsOilCommoditiesUS-Israel war on IrannewsShareReuse this content

title: Governments’ borrowing costs hit further multi-decade highs as US-Iran peace hopes fade | Government borrowing | The Guardian
description: Bond yields in US, UK, Germany France and Japan rise after ceasefire ends and Trump threatens to bomb Oman
Author: Julia Kollewe
Headline: Bond yields in US, UK, Germany France and Japan rise after ceasefire ends and Trump threatens to bomb Oman
Content: The yield, or interest rate, on the 30-year US Treasury bond rose to 5.324% on Tuesday.Photograph: Angela Weiss/AFP/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe yield, or interest rate, on the 30-year US Treasury bond rose to 5.324% on Tuesday.Photograph: Angela Weiss/AFP/Getty ImagesGovernment borrowingGovernments’ borrowing costs hit further multi-decade highs as US-Iran peace hopes fadeBond yields in US, UK, Germany France and Japan rise after ceasefire ends and Trump threatens to bomb OmanBusiness live – latest updatesJulia KolleweandGraeme WeardenTue 18 Aug 2026 06.54 EDTLast modified on Tue 18 Aug 2026 14.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGovernment borrowing costs in several advanced economies continued to rise to levels not seen in decades on Tuesday, as hopes of an end to the US-Iran war faded.Concerns about the inflation outlook worsened afterthe ceasefire between Washington DC and Tehran ended on Monday night without an agreement, with no progress on the reopening of the strait of Hormuz.Donald Trump’s threat to bomb Oman if they “get in the way” of negotiations helped topush oil higher on Tuesday, to above $91 a barrel, and investors fear higher energy prices will push inflation up, leading to higher interest rates.Cooling UK labour market ‘questions need’ for Bank of England rate hikes; grocery inflation slows to two-year low – business liveRead moreFiscal pressures are also rising as governments ramp up defence spending, which is expected to drive borrowing higher in leading European countries such as Germany and the UK.The yield, or interest rate, on the 30-year US Treasury bond rose over 5.33% on Tuesday, the highest since June 2007,adding to gains on Monday.The yield on the 10-year US Treasury bond rose above 4.74%, while the equivalent Japanese government bond yield climbed 2.5 basis points to 2.945%, the highest in three decades.The yield on the UK’s 10-year gilts rose as high as 5.176%. Germany’s 10-year bond yield rose to the highest level since 2011 while France’s equivalent hit a 16-year peak. Bond yields rise when the price of the debt falls.“Rising long-dated bond yields are not driven solely by expectations of higher interest rates and inflation fears. They can also reflect concerns around high levels of government borrowing and investors demanding greater compensation for the risks of holding long-dated government bonds,” Dan Coatsworth, the head of markets at AJ Bell, said.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toBusiness TodayGet set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morningEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionConcerns about the amount of new debt hitting the bond markets, issued by governments and companies such as AI firms, is another factor pushing up yields.“We are seeing bond yields across developed markets strike multi-year highs as fixed income investors grow nervous about a range of factors, from inflation and the Iran conflict to deeper structural concerns and fiscal worries. Issuance is clearly a factor – both on the government side (they can’t stop spending!) and on the corporate side (AI capex),” said Neil Wilson, a Saxo UK investor strategist.Explore more on these topicsGovernment borrowingEconomicsBondsGlobal economyStock marketsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Israel withdraws support for embattled Fifa president Gianni Infantino | Gianni Infantino | The Guardian
description: The Israel Football Association blamed an ‘unprecedented crisis of confidence’ and lack of ‘proper vision’ in retracting its backing for Fifa’s Gianni Infantino
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: The Israel Football Association blamed an ‘unprecedented crisis of confidence’ and lack of ‘proper vision’ in retracting its backing for Fifa’s Gianni Infantino
Content: Gianni Infantino (centre) tried to stage a photo between IFA vice-president Basim Sheikh Suliman (left) and Jibril Rajoub, president of the Palestinian Football Association.Photograph: Jennifer Gauthier/ReutersView image in fullscreenGianni Infantino (centre) tried to stage a photo between IFA vice-president Basim Sheikh Suliman (left) and Jibril Rajoub, president of the Palestinian Football Association.Photograph: Jennifer Gauthier/ReutersGianni InfantinoIsrael withdraws support for embattled Fifa president Gianni InfantinoIFA points to ‘unprecedented crisis of confidence’Premier League chief says Infantino ‘hit self-destruct’Matt HughesandNick AmesTue 18 Aug 2026 14.03 EDTLast modified on Tue 18 Aug 2026 19.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGianni Infantino’s decision to sack his chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, after the Frenchman’s criticism of the World Cup sell-off plan has hardened some opposition to the Fifa president, with the efforts to force him out expected to intensify over the next few days.On TuesdayIsraelbecame the latest Fifa member to officially withdraw their support for Infantino’s re-election in a letter sent by the head of the Israel Football Association (IFA), Moshe Zuares.Infantino ally insists Fifa president still has backing of most football associationsRead moreThe move is not a surprise as the IFA has been a member of Uefa since 1994 and Zuares sits on the European governing body’s executive committee, but it remains another blow to Infantino, who has invested significant political capital in attempting to improve sporting relations with Palestine.At Fifa’s congress in April Infantino tried to stage a photo involving the two delegations in Vancouver, but the Palestinian Football Federation president, Jibril Rajoub, refused to stand alongside IFA ⁠vice-president, Basim Sheikh ⁠Suliman. Undeterred by this setback, Infantino wants Israel and Palestine to compete in the first match of a new under-15 tournament in the United States next month, as reported by the Guardian in June.In his letter, which has been seen by the Guardian, Zuares says recent events have triggered an “unprecedented crisis of confidence” between the visions of Uefa and Fifa when it comes to global governance, adding that the rift is “profound, substantive, and principled, and compelling all stakeholders to reconsider the path forward”.In a decision he described as being taken unanimously after a meeting of the IFA’s board, Zuares confirmed: “We have no choice but to retract our previous letter of support, in the sincere hope that fruitful dialogue among all parties will eventually restore a shared, proper vision and direction for world football.”Israeli’s intervention echoes the withdrawal of support from other Uefa members including England, Wales, Scotland and the Republic of Ireland, and followed confirmation on Monday night that Lamour had left Fifa, having been deeply critical of Infantino’s Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.“If that means I lose my job, then so be it,” he said prophetically in a statement on 31 July. “I will understand and respect that decision. At least I’ll sleep well tonight.”Another Uefa executive committee member, the former Wales Women international Laura McAllister, said the decision to sack Lamour “sends a deeply troubling message” and casts serious doubt over any efforts by the global governing body to recalibrate after the FFE scandal.McAllister, who is one of five Uefa vice-presidents and worked there with Lamour before his move to Fifa in 2024, praised her former colleague for standing up to Infantino’s doomed scheme. “During the shabby events of the past weeks, he showed himself to be a courageous advocate for the most important stakeholders in football,” she said in a statement. “Kevin’s sacking seriously weakens Fifa’s administration, while undermining this unique opportunity to shift the culture at Fifa and to reset the organisation on sporting values, not simply commercial and financial ones.“Fifa is not the president, it is the whole football family. As I have said repeatedly, world football needs strong, principled, independent leaders who are prepared to speak up, challenge when necessary, and stand firmly by their values and those of the global game. Instead, the loss of a leader of Kevin’s calibre sends a deeply troubling message to all of us seeking change.”View image in fullscreenRichard Masters, the Premier League chief executive, said: ‘I don’t think Fifa should be ever contemplating selling off a stake in the World Cup.’Photograph: Mike Egerton/PAMeanwhile, Richard Masters, the Premier League chief executive, told the BBC that Infantino pressed the “self-destruct button” over his botched plan to bring private investment into theWorld Cup.“This is a problem of Fifa’s making,” Masters said. “This is a self-inflicted wound. The organisation has pressed the self-destruct button, and the consequences of that flow now into the solutions that need to be found.“I don’t think Fifa should be ever contemplating selling off a stake in the World Cup. They’re a not-for-profit organisation. They should really be holding that competition in trust for the future of football.”Explore more on these topicsGianni InfantinoFifaWorld CupFootball politicsIsrael (Football)Israel (World news)newsShareReuse this content

title: The rise and fall of Tony Romo: what comes next for CBS’s $180m NFL analyst? | US sports media | The Guardian
description: The former Dallas Cowboys star is on indefinite leave after being arrested on suspicion of drunk driving. His future in a competitive business is now in doubt
Author: Tom Dart
Headline: The former Dallas Cowboys star is on indefinite leave after being arrested on suspicion of drunk driving. His future in a competitive business is now in doubt
Content: Tony Romo, pictured at the Super Bowl in 2024, has become one of the NFL’s most prominent broadcasters.Photograph: CBS Photo Archive/CBS/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenTony Romo, pictured at the Super Bowl in 2024, has become one of the NFL’s most prominent broadcasters.Photograph: CBS Photo Archive/CBS/Getty ImagesUS sports mediaThe rise and fall of Tony Romo: what comes next for CBS’s $180m NFL analyst?The former Dallas Cowboys star is on indefinite leave after being arrested on suspicion of drunk driving. His future in a competitive business is now in doubtTom DartTue 18 Aug 2026 05.00 EDTLast modified on Tue 18 Aug 2026 20.08 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAfter Tony Romo’sarrestlast month, TMZ published a 31-minute“extended cut”of the body-camera footage from the Wisconsin police officer who arrested CBS Sports’ star NFL analyst on suspicion of operating a vehicle while under the influence.It’s an uncanny watch. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback’s familiar goofy geniality collides with the gravity and stilted formality of an encounter with law enforcement. The video of a disoriented Romo struggling to answer basic questions and failing a field sobriety test, and his rictus-grinning, disheveled, head-askew mug-shot, form a glaring contrast with his smart-suited looka year earlier: beaming as he posed in the spotlight with his play-by-play partner, Jim Nantz, at the network’s preseason media preview.Romo initially told the officer he had not been drinking before saying he had had a single Corona. He has not issued a public statement on the incident since.CBS Sports chief says ‘no timetable’ on Tony Romo’s future after OWI arrestRead moreThe arrest and the attention mean that one of the best-known television personalities in American sport will start the season as a color commentator in a grey area. Romo was scheduled to be in Minnesota on 13 September to call the game between the Vikings and the Green Bay Packers on the first Sunday of the season. Instead he is on indefinite leave and former Houston Texans star JJ Watt has been promoted from CBS’s second-tier crew to call the game with Nantz.Every week matters given the NFL’s short season but it’s unlikely that CBS will determine Romo’s future before his court date on 21 September. Unusually among US states, Wisconsin typically treats a first-offense DUI as a civil rather than a criminal offense. This is an important distinction in law, and perhaps in Romo’s employment contract, but less relevant in the court of public opinion.The incident is another strike against a 46-year-old broadcaster who has lately drawn scrutiny for aquestionable work ethic, according to the Athletic, as well as occasionalon-air gaffesand apparently waning skills. While Tom Brady has grown into his Fox Sports role after a wooden start, Romo’s analytical talentarguably diminishedas seasons passed, rosters refreshed and his first-hand knowledge of the league’s teams, players and coaches became outdated.Born in California and raised in Wisconsin, Romo spent all 13 years of his NFL career with the Cowboys and rose from relative obscurity to become one of the league’s biggest names. He was a star at the NCAA second-tier Eastern Illinois University yet went unselected in the 2003 draft. Still, he signed for Dallas as a free agent. Initially a raw third-stringer, he spent three-and-a-half seasons as a back-up before seizing his chance in 2006 when the struggling veteran Drew Bledsoe squandered the starting job. Although his career never reached Hall of Fame levels, he remains the franchise’s leader in career passing touchdowns, a remarkable achievement for an undrafted player from a small school.CBS hired Romo immediately after he retired in 2017. Eyebrows were elevated by the network’s then-rare decision to slot an untested broadcaster into a lead position but the gamble quickly paid off. Though Romo never reached a Super Bowl and had a record of two wins and four losses in the playoffs, he turned out to be a fresh and telegenic character who delivered insights andhighly accuratein-game play predictions that drewrave reviews.In 2020 CBS handed Romo a then-record 10-year, $180m contract: about $53m more than he earned during hisplaying career. It was evidence of his appeal as well as the network’s desire to keep him away from rivals such as ESPN. The former Dallas quarterback Troy Aikman signed a five-year, $90m contract with ESPN in 2022. But the $18m-a-year benchmark did not last long:that yearBrady, a singular figure who was still playing,agreedto a 10-year, $375m deal to talk for Fox Sports once he retired.View image in fullscreenTony Romo rose from an undrafted free agent to become one of the Cowboys’ finest quarterbacks.Photograph: Matthew Emmons/USA Today SportsThese amounts may seem extravagant – because they are – but are comprehensible in the context of the NFL’s importance to the networks and the broader sums at stake. CBS shells out $2.1bn a year to air games. Even this isn’t enough for the league, which hasreportedlybeen seeking a 50% increase in rights payments.“Everyone thinks they can do this job. Trust me, it’s harder than it looks. A lot harder than it looks. There’s 17 people screaming in your ear while you’re talking,” says Patrick Crakes, a media consultant who tested contenders in his former role as a Fox Sports executive. “When Romo’s at his best, he understands the game, he sees it and he can articulate it quickly and lots of times he narrows down the possibilities to two or three, he picks one and he’s right a lot.”Predicting his fate now is far from easy. Discussing the fall of Romo on 11 August, the CBS Sports president David Bersontold reportersthere is “no timetable” to decide his future. “We had to consider the impact on our image and on our brand. That’s very important to us. Whether the games, marketing, PR, social, the focus should and needs to be on our presentation and not on any other factors,” he said.Aside from issues of morality, loyalty and reputation, a ruthlessly pragmatic calculation could also enter the picture: if Watt proves a success, perhaps the network will conclude it makes sense to cut a fading Romo and potentially save $72m if the rest of his contract can be voided on the basis that the drunk-driving charge damaged the network’s reputation. Another possibility is that Romo returns to air with CBS at some point this season or next, but on the “B” team, calling less attractive match-ups.Industry standards have undeniably evolved. Though Howard Cosell’s drinking – said to occur before, after and even during broadcasts – was an open secret, the great ABC sportscaster’s consumption did not preclude him from a long and storied career, nor was it widely publicized until a former ABC executivewrote a bookin 1988 that alleged Cosell threw up on his co-commentator’s cowboy boots in the booth after imbibing too much vodka before a Monday Night Football broadcast in 1970. (Cosell, who left the stadium at half-time, claimed he was sick with a virus.)Will Romo’s troubles dissuade networks from giving out lavish contracts in the future? Crakes doubts that executives will be rushing to offer more decade-long deals – not because of Romo’s personal travails but since today’s media landscape is so turbulent, making future rights deals and negotiating leverage hard to predict. CBS’s parent company, Paramount Skydance, wants to acquire Warner Bros Discovery in a potential$110bn dealthat could see CBS Sports merge with TNT Sports.CBS was themost-watchedNFL broadcaster last season according to Nielsen ratings, with an average of 25.8 million viewers for its late Sunday afternoon games. Its Thanksgiving clash between the Cowboys and the Kansas City Chiefs attracted an average of 57.2 million viewers – thelargest-everaudience for an NFL regular-season contest.Such huge figures, especially remarkable at a time when traditional broadcast television is in decline, underline the value of the NFL to the legacy networks. They explain why charismatic personalities such as Romo who can elucidate a complex sport for mainstream audiences are able to command vast salaries. Constant scrutiny and high expectations are part of the bargain. “You’re really carrying the brand flag for your network, for your sport and for the league and that’s why those guys make so much money. There’s a lot of trust that goes into that,” Crakes says.If a commentator becomes divisive and derided, that’s a problem. “Football in the United States is the most general market product that we have any more. It’s the closest thing to going to blockbuster movies that you can find,” Crakes adds. “It’s the closest thing we’ve got any more in the United States to talking to everybody.”Explore more on these topicsUS sports mediaNFLCBSUS television industryUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Barcelona steal Rodri away from Real Madrid and plan to make him new Busquets | Barcelona | The Guardian
description: Spain’s World Cup-winning captain has completed his move to Camp Nou where he is a natural successor to club legend
Author: Sid Lowe
Headline: Spain’s World Cup-winning captain has completed his move to Camp Nou where he is a natural successor to club legend
Content: ‘I’m happy to be here’: Rodri poses with a Barcelona shirt at his official unveiling.Photograph: Quique García/EPAView image in fullscreen‘I’m happy to be here’: Rodri poses with a Barcelona shirt at his official unveiling.Photograph: Quique García/EPABarcelonaBarcelona steal Rodri away from Real Madrid and plan to make him new BusquetsSpain’s World Cup-winning captain has completed his move to Camp Nou where he is a natural successor to club legendSid LoweTue 18 Aug 2026 15.49 EDTLast modified on Tue 18 Aug 2026 18.09 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBy the time Flight PTN27B started its descent into El Prat a bit before 8pm on Monday evening, a small crowd had gathered by the terminal doors, waiting for it to land. A few people stood and watched the sky, cameras out to capture its arrival. A lot more watched on their phones. In the two hours it had taken to get there from Manchester, taking off at 5.11pm, 101 minutes behind schedule, the Pilatus PC-24 had become the most tracked plane on the planet. Everyone knew that Rodrigo Hernández was on board. Unless, of course, he had been sneaked away in a catering cart.Five days earlier, Rodri had been seen, and recorded, at Barajas airport waiting to get on a flight back to Manchester from Madrid. He wheeled a small RFEF (Spanish football federation) case with his name on, stood alone in the queue, the World Cup-winning captain just a bloke in shorts and T-shirt, and his stay in the UK was supposed to be brief, just long enough to say goodbye. The plane he was boarding was a Ryanair one: that was the detail everyone homed in on, something extraordinary in the ordinariness. This time, though, he came on a private jet, one way. His family travelled with him. He came to sign for FCBarcelona.Rodri calls it ‘a dream to play for Barcelona’ as he flies in for medicalRead moreRodri was late: an agreement betweenManchester Cityand Barcelona had taken a little longer than expected, long enough for concern to creep in, and his flight landed 70 minutes behind schedule. Maybe he islate-late, too: at 30, and three years after the departure of Sergio Busquets – the man to whom he had always been likened and whose natural successor he has always been … this transfer could perhaps have come sooner. Yet it was rarely even contemplated, virtually up until the moment it happened. In that sense, it had actually been quick. A fortnight ago, few thought of this.Now here he was, heading out in jeans and a white T-shirt. There was expectation, a hint still of disbelief that they had got him. A touch of relief, too, after the delay. They had been “intense days”, Rodri said, but now it was done. Barcelona’s third bid had been accepted: €60m plus a further €15m in add-ons, €11m of which are virtually guaranteed. He will earn around €15m a year, an increase on his salary at City, and has signed a four-year deal.Quick GuideRodri seals Barcelona transferShowThe Spain midfielder Rodri has completed his €60m move from Manchester City to Barcelona, signing a four-year contract after undergoing a medical on Tuesday."Barcelona and Manchester City have reached an agreement for Rodri, who is committing to the Catalan club until 30 June 2030," read a club statement.Barça added that the 30-year-old is "considered one of the best players in the world in his position", and "stands out for his tactical intelligence, composure on the ball, ability to regain possession and precision in his passing".Rodri (pictured) was named the best player of the World Cup after Spain’s triumph this summer. He spent seven seasons at the Etihad Stadium, winning the Premier League four times and scoring the winner in the 2023 Champions League final against Inter. The 2024 Ballon d'Or winner joined from Atlético Madrid in July 2019, and was in the final year of his contract.In a message to City fans on the club’s website, Rodri wrote: "I found that saying goodbye is one of the most difficult things in life but I am going to try. I knew I came into a top team but I never thought we could be able to create the legacy we made – winning trophies, fans around the world, love and respect."We made an example to inspire the next generations not only because the success, also because the way we did it," he added. "And the fans were with us every step of the way. City didn’t just make me grow as a player. They made me grow as a human ... Manchester shaped my whole life. It’s time to say goodbye, thanks to the club, the fans, the staff and my teammates. This journey couldn’t be the same without you, my heart will always be blue."Barcelona saw an initial £40m offer and an increased bid turned down before an agreement was struck on Sunday. Rodri flew to Barcelona’s El Prat airport on Monday and told reporters: "Playing for Barcelona is a dream come true for me."The new City manager, Enzo Maresca, faces a race to rebuild his midfield, with Rodri joining Bernardo Silva in departing the club, Tijjani Reijnders poised to join Saudi Pro League side Al Qadsiah, and Newcastle reportedly interested in Nico González. Elliot Anderson has joined from Nottingham Forest for £116m and City have been linked with Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi and Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández.Photograph: Quality Sport Images/Getty Images EuropeWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.“I’m happy to be here,” Rodri said, and they were happy to have him. The following morning he arrived at the club’s Joan Despí training ground to complete his medical, everything signed off. As he left the terminal building, Rodri had been asked if this was a dream come true. He of course said yes it was, which he had to say. The question had been direct, leading. It had been loaded too.A Ballon d’Or winner and the embodiment of a style, an identity, that is theirs too, Rodri is the perfect fit. The time was right for him too. Voted the best player at the World Cup, the culmination of his recovery from injury, there was just one year left on his contract at City. He had won it all in England and Pep Guardiola had gone. After seven years away, home called. But home didn’t mean Barcelona; in fact, it had seemed more likely to mean Real Madrid.View image in fullscreenRodri lifts the World Cup after Spain’s victory over Argentina.Photograph: Image Photo Agency/Getty ImagesRodri grew up to the north-west of the capital and even Real’s refusal to turn up the night he won the Ballon d’Or, an act of grubbiness and disrespect, didn’t mean closing the door. Instead, he was increasingly open about his willingness – his apparent desire – to go. “Obviously, when the best club in history, the most successful with everything that brings, call you it is an honour and you always have to pay attention,” he said not long after the ceremony. In the spring, Rodri admitted he would like to return to Spain and that he would not rule out going to Real, even if he had been in the academy at Atlético. When Real held presidential elections in May, the pretender, Enrique Riquelme, announced that his signing would be Rodri. For his part, Rodri kept his counsel and come the end of the World Cup he had three offers: Paris Saint-Germain, who he ruled out because he wanted a return to Spain, Barcelona and Real.Real, ambivalent before, appeared convinced by his status as the World Cup’s best player, president Florentino Pérez’s reticence seemingly overcome. He wasexactlythe footballer they needed, someone to get them to actually play, and Real were confident that he would come, that theirs was the only real offer. One headline summed it up: “Rodri is next”. This was done, which is when things tend to get undone. Rodri had an offer that was impossible to turn down. Only the terms of the negotiation shifted, doubts growing about Real’s commitment, frustration growing.Barcelona, seeing an opportunity, pushed at an unexpectedly opening door. Rodri might not have been the player they needed most – a forward was their priority – but, well, he’s Rodri. This was undeniably a step up in quality, even for a midfield like theirs. Meanwhile, doubts over Frenkie de Jong’s fitness brought a reframing: maybe he was more necessary than they had believed. Likewise, that slight nagging doubt about his fit with Pedri in theselecciónfeels like a small one, easily overcome, certainly no obstacle to bringing together arguably the best two midfielders in the world. Good luck getting the ball off them.On the day that Real announced ViníciusJúnior had renewed his contract at the club and that they had made Yan Diomande the most expensive signing in their history, they also briefed that Rodri wasn’t coming after all. The excitement among fans at the Santiago Bernabéu turned to disappointment, a kind of lingering doom. That huge hole in the middle of Madrid’s midfield was still not plugged, their issues still not addressed.View image in fullscreenRodri enjoyed seven successful seasons at Manchester City.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAFor Barcelona this was the signing of the summer. The World Cup winning-captain, perhaps the best player on the planet, was coming to Catalonia. There was a kind of gleeful disbelief, the expectation huge. Rodri thanked Madrid, but he had made his decision. As usual, Jorge Valdano put it best when the €75m deal had been done. “Rodri’s deal is worth €35m for what it gives Barcelona and €40m for what it takes away from Madrid,” he said. “At Real Madrid he would have revolutionised their play and improved everything.”Valdano added he will not have the impact on Barcelona’s style that he would have had on Real’s, but that was because it is already his. “I always try to learn from Busquets,” said Rodri. “I watched him especially closely: he, and others, laid down a model of playing I knew I had to follow.” When Rodri joined City, Guardiola had found his other Busquets, or so it goes. Waiting patiently for his moment, when Busquets finally left the national team, it was always going to be Rodri who stepped in. A “perfect computer”, Luis de la Fuente called him. Doing so with Barcelona would seem natural, maybe even overdue, his signing a no-brainer.Rodri’s World Cup overcame any doubts that it was too late, that his time had gone, and brought an extra dimension too, a shift in his role which he didn’t just embrace but consciously sought. He had the maturity, the leadership, the ascendancy over Spain’s young players – Barcelona’s young players – that they needed. And he needed too: there is something almost paternal about him and they had the youth that hewantedto lead, to guide. And, of course, the talent too. He knows how good it is to play with them: he had done so all summer, winning the ultimate award. And so it was done.Now all that was needed was for City and Barcelona to reach an agreement. Eventually, they did, so Rodrigo Hernández had another plane to catch.Explore more on these topicsBarcelonaManchester CityTransfer windowfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: San Diego Padres minor-league staffer detained by ICE after arrest in Texas | San Diego Padres | The Guardian
description: Padres catching coordinator was stopped at an El Paso airport while returning from a work trip as his family and DHS disputed his immigration status
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Padres catching coordinator was stopped at an El Paso airport while returning from a work trip as his family and DHS disputed his immigration status
Content: Oswaldo Pirela had been working with the El Paso Chihuahuas, the Padres’ Triple-A affiliate.Photograph: The Washington Post/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenOswaldo Pirela had been working with the El Paso Chihuahuas, the Padres’ Triple-A affiliate.Photograph: The Washington Post/Getty ImagesSan Diego PadresSan Diego Padres minor-league staffer detained by ICE after arrest in TexasFamily says Venezuelan has pending asylum claimDHS says 34-year-old faces removal proceedingsGuardian sportTue 18 Aug 2026 14.00 EDTLast modified on Tue 18 Aug 2026 14.03 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSan Diego Padres minor-league catching coordinator Oswaldo Pirela remained in federal immigration custody on Tuesday after being detained at an airport in El Paso, Texas, while returning from a work trip.Pirela’s family said the 34-year-old Venezuelan has a pending asylum claim and has continually renewed his work authorization. The Department of Homeland Security said he does not have legal status and will face removal proceedings.Pirela was detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) at El Paso International Airport early on Sunday, according to his relatives.His sister, Daniela Pirela,told NBC Newsthat he was stopped at about 5am. His wife, Kemberly Avila,told The Athleticthat he had been preparing to fly home to Arizona.Pirela had been working with the El Paso Chihuahuas, the Padres’ Triple-A affiliate. His family said he regularly travels for his role with the organization.“We recently became aware of the detainment of minor league catching coordinator Oswaldo Pirela in El Paso, Texas,” the Padres said in a statement. “We are working to gather additional information and will not have any further comment at this time.”Major League Baseballtold CNNthat the Padres had contacted Pirela’s family. Avila said the club was helping them and that she had spoken with her husband since his detention.According to ESPN, Pirela’s brother said he was not carrying his physical work-permit card when he was stopped. Avila told The Athletic that the family have pending asylum applications and carry temporary identification cards.Pirela arrived in the US from Venezuela and applied for asylum in 2014, his relatives said. They said he fled political persecution and has renewed his work authorization whenever it approached expiration. His family also said he is pursuing an EB-2 visa, an employment-based route to permanent residency.DHS disputed the family’s description of his immigration status. The department told CNN that Pirela entered the US illegally in 2014 and received permission to remain until February 2018. Officials said he stayed beyond that date and was not carrying documentation giving him legal status when he was approached. DHS said he would remain in ICE custody while removal proceedings continued.“Work authorization or a pending application do not confer legal status in the United States,” a DHS spokesperson said.Pirela lives outside Phoenix with Avila and their two US-born daughters. Daniela Pirela told NBC News that she had spoken with him briefly but knew little about the conditions in which he was being held.She said her brother told her he was all right, although she believed he was trying to prevent the family from worrying.Pirela joined the Padres’ player-development staff in 2024. He previously spent three seasons as a catcher in the Texas Rangers’ minor-league system, playing in the Dominican Summer League from 2009 to 2011.His detention comes amid the Trump administration’s push to accelerate deportations and expand the range of immigrants subject to arrest.MLB has previously been pulled into the administration’s immigration crackdown. Last year the Los Angeles Dodgerssaid they refused ICE agents accessto stadium parking areas during enforcement operations in the city.It was unclear on Tuesday when Pirela would next appear before an immigration court.Explore more on these topicsSan Diego PadresICE (US Immigration and Customs Enforcement)MLBBaseballUS sportsUS immigrationnewsShareReuse this content

title: Williams sisters come unstuck in Cincinnati in first doubles outing together since 2022 | Tennis | The Guardian
description: Serena and Venus Williams took to the doubles court together for the first time since the 2022 US Open but lost to Payton Stearns and Marta Kostyuk
Author: Tumaini Carayol
Headline: Serena and Venus Williams took to the doubles court together for the first time since the 2022 US Open but lost to Payton Stearns and Marta Kostyuk
Content: Venus and Serena Williams during the first round of the women’s doubles tournament at the Cincinnati Open.Photograph: Robert Prange/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenVenus and Serena Williams during the first round of the women’s doubles tournament at the Cincinnati Open.Photograph: Robert Prange/Getty ImagesTennisWilliams sisters come unstuck in Cincinnati in first doubles outing together since 2022Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns beat American pair 6-2, 1-6, 10-8Serena and Venus enjoy ‘fun’ on-court reunion despite defeatTumaini Carayolat the Lindner Family Tennis CenterTue 18 Aug 2026 00.24 EDTLast modified on Tue 18 Aug 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleOne game into the family reunion of the decade,Venus Williamslaunched herself inside the baseline in her single-minded pursuit of a puffball second serve. For a brief moment the Cincinnati Open was transported back 15 years. Williams pounded her forehand return directly at the right hip of her opponent Marta Kostyuk, instantly eliciting gasps from the audience as she snatched the point. Back when the Williams sisters spent their spare time racking up grand slam titles for fun, this was how they dealt with most adversaries.Arthur Fery gives Alex de Minaur stern test before bowing out in CincinnatiRead moreIn the end, Venus and Serena’s first doubles match together in four years, and only their second in the past decade, ended in a rollercoaster 6-2, 1-6, 10-8 defeat to Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns, another wildcard pair and two formidable singles players. For once, the result did not seem to matter.“Winning is obviously great,” said Serena. “But I think in this position, [we’re] just having fun. I didn’t come out here to win this tournament. Obviously, I wanted to do the best I could do, but I think having fun and also just seeing how we are and how we feel out there. Being out there with the fans, too, is just really good, just to give them another opportunity to see us play, which is really cool.”Even before she made the familiar trip to Mason, Ohio, Serena’s presence had been felt this year. For two days during the first round, a plane circled above the tournament grounds carrying an advertisement banner featuring Serena endorsing Ro, a telehealth company that provides patients with access to GLP-1 weight-loss drugs.View image in fullscreenSerena Williams hits a forehand.Photograph: Scott Stuart/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockThis match also quietly underlined how dysfunctional professional tennis can be. Despite the massive anticipation surrounding the return of the Williams sisters – almost certainly the last time this audience will get to see them – the rigid nature of television contracts meant the match was relegated to Grandstand Court, the tournament’s 5,000-seat second stadium. Every seat was taken, with fans streaming out of the entrances and crowding the winding staircase from the adjoining Center Court, which holds 11,600, to catch a glimpse of two American greats.For all the goodwill, excitement and anticipation at the simple joy of seeing them together again, early on the spectacle itself was rough. After Venus held in the opening game, they conceded five consecutive games to trail 1-5. Serena’s lack of matchplay was the most obvious issue, with the younger sister struggling to find hertiming on her groundstrokes or rhythm on her usually immaculate serve.As Serena’s rust gradually fell away, Venus was largely solid, pairing crisp shotmaking with elite reflex volleys. By the start of set two, everything was flowing. They rolled through the set and into a match tie‑break. Down 2-8, they nearly pulled off an outlandish comeback before a double fault from Venus at 8-9 ended their hopes.View image in fullscreenMarta Kostyuk of Ukraine and Peyton Stearns of the United States.Photograph: Robert Prange/Getty ImagesSerena had not competed since her return to singles competition at Wimbledon last month, where she sustained a knee injury in her three-setloss to Maya Joint, forcing her to withdraw from her planned doubles match with Venus. “That was a little traumatic experience for me,” Serena said, smiling. “It took me two hours to leave the locker room that night and it’s been a long recovery, which is something I never thought I’d say because I never thought I’d be here sitting and talking to you all again. But, you know, what doesn’t kill you makes you stronger.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIn her Instagram post after the loss, which included photos of vials she had used to collect the fluid from her knee, Serena said her followers would see her soon on a court near them, and here she made good on that. The US Open will follow for both sisters, but it is unclear whether they will take to the court in singles or doubles. “I’ve never really enjoyed the process, but I think this time I’m enjoying the process a little bit more than I ever have,” said Serena. “It’s kind of just having a different view of it. And it’s also like this isn’t for ever. This is like not long. So it’s also just fun to know that too. And like I’m not playing every week. I’m not showing up every week and have kids. So it’s a little bit different.”Serena’s comeback, which has mainly been confined to the doubles court so far, has served as a reminder of the greatness of the Williams sisters’ doubles careers, achievements that are usually hidden behind their all-time great singles results. This is also one of the greatest doubles teams in history. They have won 14 grand slam titles together – winning every one of their grand slam finals – which places them joint-second in the open era among women’s doubles teams, behind Martina Navratilova and Pam Shriver. They also reached world No 1 and won three Olympic gold medals.Their partnership began in the 1990s, yet still it endures. “I think we waited a long time to get back on the doubles court, even this year,” said Venus. “I think eventually we would find our way to each other.”Explore more on these topicsTennisSerena WilliamsVenus WilliamsUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: In Zavier Gozo, Crystal Palace land a US prospect living up to the hype | Crystal Palace | The Guardian
description: The 19-year-old US youth international has turned heads in MLS this year, and is on the cusp of a USMNT breakthrough
Author: Jeff Rueter
Headline: The 19-year-old US youth international has turned heads in MLS this year, and is on the cusp of a USMNT breakthrough
Content: Zavier Gozo has been a standout performance for Real Salt Lake this season.Photograph: Al Sermeno/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenZavier Gozo has been a standout performance for Real Salt Lake this season.Photograph: Al Sermeno/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesCrystal PalaceIn Zavier Gozo, Crystal Palace land a US prospect living up to the hypeThe 19-year-old US youth international has turned heads in MLS this year, and is on the cusp of a USMNT breakthroughJeff RueterTue 18 Aug 2026 17.32 EDTLast modified on Tue 18 Aug 2026 17.34 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFor much of the past year, the story of American starlet Zavier Gozo has been one of realizing potential – even in failure. Speaking with the Guardian the day after he and Real Salt Lake teammate Diego Lunalearnedthey wouldn’t be on Mauricio Pochettino’s squad for this summer’s World Cup, the 19-year-old Gozo admitted the rejection made him realize how close he’d gotten to earning a spot.“I thought I would be less disappointed than I was,”Gozo saidin May. “Obviously, it wasn’t like I was supposed to go. I feel like I was disappointed, but I also think it just gave me so much more motivation to be able to make the first team, whenever that is.”From media deals to roster rules: five priorities for MLS’s new commissionerRead moreIf it works out well, Gozo’s move to Crystal Palace could see that happen sooner than many would have anticipated a year ago. ThePremier Leagueclub finalized the transfer of Gozo from Real Salt Lake on Tuesday in a five-year deal. The agreement is reportedly worth around $15m (£11m).The move follows one of the most rapid ascents of any American men’s prospect in recent memory.Gozo joined theReal Salt Lakeacademy in 2021 at age 14, debuting with their second team, Real Monarchs, a year later. His MLS debut came in 2023, when he was still just 16. Over time, Gozo emerged as an option at right wing-back offering precocious confidence on the ball, capping his first full season with RSL with four goals and three assists in 1,810 minutes.This season, Gozo has been given increased license to stay upfield. His technique in close quarters has been especially impressive, with deft touches and passes helping RSL get into dangerous areas. His end product has also been on greater display, with six goals and five assists in 1,417 minutes thus far.Zavier Gozo Real Salt Lake highlightsHis ability to set up his own shot as well as create dangerous looks for his teammates helps him stand out. Gozo has made 67 progressive carries upfield, per Futi, a category led by Lionel Messi, Denis Bouanga, Evander and Anders Dreyer – four members of last year’sMLSBest XI.The question for any young player of Gozo’s caliber is how best to position themselves for international consideration. On the one hand, he had already established himself as a regular starter in MLS. On the other, strong performances in MLS – as in any league – provide no guarantee of landing on a national team, as Gozo’s teammate Luna learned the hard way by being among Pochettino’s toughest omissions.As a result, Gozo felt he was nearing the ideal window for making a move across the Atlantic.“I feel like I’m ready to go,” Gozo addedwithout hesitation. “Whether that happens or not, I don’t know, but I think this is a unique situation I have. I’m blessed to be in a situation where I have such a good club to be at, but I also think, you know … What’s next in my career? I don’t know.”The son of an American mother and an Ivorian father, Gozo also earned his first US youth international callup in 2022, beginning with the U-15s. He has become a regular with the youth national teams.With Pochettino opting to stick with the USMNT through the 2030 World Cup, Gozo figures to be in contention with the players who made the squad for this summer’s tournament for a place in the US’s plans over the next four years. Training at Palace every day with US mainstay Chris Richards will surely keep him in Pochettino’s sights, to say nothing of any Premier League minutes he’s able to get under new manager Pierre Sage.Explore more on these topicsCrystal PalaceReal Salt LakePremier LeagueUSAMLSfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Jamal Musiala says ‘treatable seizures’ are reason for two collapses in four days | Bayern Munich | The Guardian
description: The Bayern Munich winger Jamal Musiala has said ‘neurological dysfunction’ and ‘treatable seizures’ have caused two on-field collapses in quick succession
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The Bayern Munich winger Jamal Musiala has said ‘neurological dysfunction’ and ‘treatable seizures’ have caused two on-field collapses in quick succession
Content: Jamal Musiala is helped from the field by a Bayern Munich doctor after falling to the ground during their game at Heidenheim.Photograph: EyesWideOpen/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJamal Musiala is helped from the field by a Bayern Munich doctor after falling to the ground during their game at Heidenheim.Photograph: EyesWideOpen/Getty ImagesBayern MunichJamal Musiala says ‘treatable seizures’ are reason for two collapses in four daysMusiala reveals ‘neurological dysfunction’ diagnosisWinger has fallen to floor during two recent friendliesPA Media and AFPTue 18 Aug 2026 16.08 EDTLast modified on Tue 18 Aug 2026 18.36 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTheBayern Munichwinger Jamal Musiala has revealed he is suffering from “treatable absence seizures” after he collapsed on the pitch for the second time in four days.Musiala fell to the floor eight minutes after coming on as a substitute in Bayern’s friendly with Heidenheim on Tuesday night. The 23-year-old experienced a similar incident during Saturday’s friendly against RB Leipzig, but Musiala has insisted there is no long-term health risk.“First things first, I am doing well. I am incredibly grateful for your messages and your support!” Musialaposted on Instagram. “I understand that many of you are worried. I would like to put those concerns to rest today and explain the situation.“I have been diagnosed with brief, temporary – but treatable – absence seizures resulting from a neurological dysfunction. These can lead to the kind of incidents seen recently, such as during the match against Leipzig or the game in Heidenheim.“I know they might look alarming at first glance, but for me, they are currently part of my everyday life. I am receiving excellent medical care and remain very optimistic. FC Bayern and my personal support network are right by my side, helping me through this. Importantly, there is no further health risk involved.”View image in fullscreenJamal Musiala also had to leave the field during Bayern Munich’s friendly win over RB Leipzig on Saturday.Photograph: Midori Ikenouchi/DeFodi Images/ShutterstockThe Germany international added: “In close consultation and regular contact with the experts, it was my personal wish to face this challenge; with the medical clearance of the neurologists, I want to continue doing what helps my recovery most: simply living my life and pursuing my passion for playing football.”Having come on for Ismael Saibari after 61 minutes against Heidenheim, Musiala was replaced by Cassiano Kiala eight minutes later. He appeared dazed as he received medical treatment and was helped off the pitch, with Bayern’s sporting director, Max Eberl, moving to play down concerns soon after the game.“Jamal will speak about this in the near future. We knew about it and we are aware of the situation,” Eberl said.Bayern won the game 4-2, with Felipe Chávez, Arijon Ibrahimovic, Luis Díaz and Nathaniel Brown all on target. Musiala also required medical attention after collapsing in the match against RB Leipzig.Explore more on these topicsBayern MunichnewsShareReuse this content

title: Jeanie Buss reportedly attempting to halt her siblings’ attempt to sell remaining stake in Lakers | Los Angeles Lakers | The Guardian
description: Jeanie Buss is reportedly challenging her siblings’ attempt to sell the family’s remaining stake in the Los Angeles Lakers
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Jeanie Buss is reportedly challenging her siblings’ attempt to sell the family’s remaining stake in the Los Angeles Lakers
Content: Jeanie Buss’s family have owned at least part of the Lakers since 1970s.Photograph: Allen J Schaben/Los Angeles Times/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJeanie Buss’s family have owned at least part of the Lakers since 1970s.Photograph: Allen J Schaben/Los Angeles Times/Getty ImagesLos Angeles LakersJeanie Buss reportedly attempting to halt her siblings’ attempt to sell remaining stake in LakersJeanie Buss wants to remain as controlling ownerFamily were set to sell stake to Bob Iger and Josh KushnerReutersMon 17 Aug 2026 23.19 EDTLast modified on Tue 18 Aug 2026 09.51 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleJeanie Buss is reportedly challenging her siblings’ attempt to sell the family’s remaining stake in theLos Angeles Lakers.Hours after the Buss family released a statement revealing their ⁠intention to sell their 17.8% ownership of the franchise to Bob Iger and Josh Kushner,CNBC and ESPN reportedthat Jeanie Buss’s lawyer sought to halt her siblings’ sale on ⁠legal grounds.At issue is Jeanie ⁠Buss’s status as ​the Lakers’ controlling owner.NBAguidelines require controlling owners or governors to own at least 15% of a franchise.The Lakers have become a poker chip for some of the most powerful men in AmericaRead moreFourteen months ago, Jeanie Buss spearheaded the sale of the franchise to ⁠Mark Walterfor $10bn, a then-record for a US sports franchise. The Buss family trust – which is comprised of Jerry Buss’s six children – voted to sell to Walter, although there was some infighting due ⁠to the perception that the process was rushed. Part of the agreement with Walter provided that Jeanie Buss would remain governor through 2030, but ​her siblings were terminated from their positions with the ‌organization following the sale.Last week, Walter ‌sold the Lakers to Iger and Kushnerfor the record-breaking price of $12.5bn, a sale that has not yet been approved ‌by the NBA.The Buss family – who have been either a primary or minority owner of the Lakers since 1979 – made their move Monday afternoon, though it wasn’t clear at the time that Jeanie Buss was against the deal.“We have decided as a family to sell the remaining Buss Family Trust shares to the Bob Iger group as part of the ongoing transaction,” the family said in a statement to ESPN. “We love the Lakers, Laker fans and will continue ‌to support Los Angeles; but it is time to use this opportunity to move on and exit gracefully while we still can.”Lawyer Adam Streisand replied on Jeanie Buss’s behalf later Monday, with a letter obtained by ​CNBC and ESPN addressed to her siblings, Jim, Johnny, Janie, Joey and Jesse. Streisand argued that a court ruled in 2017 that any sale of the Lakers required approval from the co-trustees, Jeanie among them.“Pursuant to the JAB Trust and the attached Court Order,” Streisand added, “the co-trustees are bound to vote the Los Angeles Lakers, Inc. shares to ensure that the minimum 15% ownership requirement is ⁠maintained in order to ensure that Jeanie Buss may remain Controlling Owner. Any attempt by the co-trustees ​to do otherwise, and any attempt ​to aid or abet the co-trustees as such, ​would constitute a breach of trust, breach of fiduciary duty and be in contempt of court.”Jeanie Buss ​took over for her ‌late father as governor ​of the Lakers in 2013.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionWalter, ​the CEO and chair of diversified holding company TWG Global, owns MLB’s Los Angeles Dodgers and the WNBA’s Los Angeles Sparks. He is under federal investigation for alleged tax fraud involving four of his other business interests.Should the sale go through, Iger and Kushner will own approximately 83% of the Lakers.The NBA board of governors, which must approve this sale, does not meet until 15 September in New ‌York.Explore more on these topicsLos Angeles LakersNBAWest CoastBasketballUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Chelsea’s boardroom rift: if Boehly goes who will Clearlake have left to blame? | Chelsea | The Guardian
description: Despite another reset with a new manager and fresh strategy, the boardroom drama persists at Stamford Bridge
Author: Sam Cunningham
Headline: Despite another reset with a new manager and fresh strategy, the boardroom drama persists at Stamford Bridge
Content: Chelsea co-owner Todd Boehly (centre) may end his five-year tenure at Chelsea to leave Clearlake Capital with total control.Photograph: Adam Davy/PAView image in fullscreenChelsea co-owner Todd Boehly (centre) may end his five-year tenure at Chelsea to leave Clearlake Capital with total control.Photograph: Adam Davy/PAChelseaAnalysisChelsea’s boardroom rift: if Boehly goes who will Clearlake have left to blame?Sam CunninghamDespite another reset with a new manager and fresh strategy, the boardroom drama persists at Stamford BridgeTue 18 Aug 2026 12.53 EDTLast modified on Tue 18 Aug 2026 21.30 EDTSharePerhaps, in hindsight, it was always going to end this way. As some of the world’s wealthiest investors scrambled to find funds after Vladimir Putin’s invasion of Ukraine set a series of dominoes toppling thatforced Roman Abramovich to sell Chelsea, it threw together some unexpected allies.Todd Boehly became the public face of the winning bid, convincing the US sports mogul Mark Walter and the Swiss businessman Hansjörg Wyss to join as 12.8% minority investors. The private equity firm Clearlake Capital put in 61.6%, bringing the owners Behdad Eghbali and José E Feliciano, who made their fortunes investing in tech, into the leadership fold.Todd Boehly and Mark Walter consider selling Chelsea shares to Clearlake CapitalRead moreBut once the adrenaline rush of beating 11 serious rivals in an expedited bid process run by the Raine Group had worn off, that was really when the problems started. Now they actually ownedChelsea, how were they going to run it? What was the strategy? How would they tackle a stadium falling well behind their rivals?Maybe Abramovich made running Chelsea look easier than it was. The club had not finished outside the top five for six seasons, yet in the four seasons since the takeover, their average league position is eighth – with a high of fourth and a low of 12th. Possibly the conflicting opinions of people who always think they are right, and have the money to prove it, is not the optimal setup.Before the takeover, an agreement was struck that Boehly, representing Walter and Wyss, would have final signoff on major decisions alongside Eghbali and Feliciano. Over the years, Boehly and Eghbali have been the dominant day-to-day decision-makers at the club, while the others remained largely silent partners, insulated from the fan anger and social media ridicule that inevitably follows any period of struggle.Some sources maintain that Boehly and Eghbali share a “professional” relationship, but signs of strain had leaked into the public domain long before this week’s revelation that Boehly and Walter wereopen to selling their stakes to Clearlakein a deal that would value the club at about £5bn.In May 2024 Boehly told the Qatar Economic Forum that “patience” with the project was essential. Mauricio Pochettino had just led Chelsea to the EFL Cup final, the FA Cup semi-final and they had recovered from a poor start to finish sixth. Cole Palmer was a breakout star; Reece James was made captain. They won their last five games of the season.View image in fullscreenXabi Alonso is aiming to rediscover the momentum Chelsea had built under Enzo Maresca.Photograph: Paul Dennis/TGS Photo/ShutterstockSix days later,Pochettino was gone– dismissed after the co-sporting directors Paul Winstanley and Laurence Stewart compiled an 18-page review of the season.Another glimpse of the pervading tension – and possibly a hint at what was to come – emerged in March last year in Boehly’s Bloomberg interview discussing the slow-moving stadium development plans, four years after they were announced.“We have to think long term about what we’re trying to accomplish,” Boehly said. “We have a big stadium development opportunity that we have to flesh out. That’s going to be where we’re either aligned or we ultimately decide to go different ways.”Publicly, Boehly insisted the ownership was aligned. Yet that is also at odds with how it began: the American installing himself as sporting director and driving a £250m spending spree targeting experienced players such as Raheem Sterling and Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang. Chelsea finished 12th.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBoehly then stepped back, with Eghbali taking a more active role. About 70 interviews took place to build a new football structure, resulting in the appointments of Winstanley and Stewart – later promoted to co-sporting directors – and Joe Shields, now a co-director of recruitment.They attempted to redefine how a football club is run: buying young, handing out unusually long contracts, in a model that has fascinated and baffled many in football. As an indication of how well that’s gone, in 2024 fans placed stickers around Stamford Bridge mocking up the three owners as clowns, while the Chelsea Supporters’ Trust described their club as “a laughing stock”.The spending has been unprecedented – the pre-tax loss of £262.4m in the year ending June 2025 was aPremier League recordsupporters had probably not envisaged after Boehly declared the owners’ vision was “to make the fans proud” after the takeover. They have complied with Premier League spending restrictions only by effectively selling the women’s side to themselves. But it could not stop a significant fine forbreaching Uefa’s financial rules, which did not permit the club to include the sale as income.But there have been signs that the grand plan(s) will work. Momentum grew under Enzo Maresca Chelsea qualified for the Champions League and lifted the Club World Cup, and there was frustration that last season was derailed by his abrupt departure in January, after which they plummeted from Champions League contenders to 10th.Now comes another reset under Xabi Alonso and a new strategy tweak towards older, more tried and tested players. But the boardroom drama persists. Both sides have explored buying each other out in recent years, but it appears Boehly’s and Walter’s hands have been forced. Walter, a long-term friend and business partner of Boehly, is under investigation by the US Department of Justice for alleged tax fraud and is believed to be selling assets to pay loans facing federal attention. He unexpectedlysold the Los Angeles Lakersto Josh Kushner and Bob Iger for $12.5bn (£9.2bn) last week and his Chelsea stake could be next.An exit would coincide neatly with Boehly’s five-year tenure as Chelsea chair coming to an end at the conclusion of this season and a representative from Clearlake ready to fill his place. If a sale is agreed, Eghbali and Feliciano will have full control – and no one else to blame if things don’t improve.Explore more on these topicsChelseaFootball politicsanalysisShareReuse this content
